title: PowerPoint: upload skills to a Brand Kit for use by Copilot in PowerPoint
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, Brand Kit permissions, licensing requirements and policy paths are supported. Minor corrections should replace the policy applicability caveats with the documented scope and reconcile the sharing and audit checklist steps with the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support uploading a skill (.md file) in Brand Kit for use within Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Upload skill (.md file) in Brand Kit and use within PPT Copilot

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-23T22:59:12.
Microsoft Support now documents sharing Brand Kit skills for use in Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Brand managers can now share skills with their organization through Brand kit for use within Copilot in PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Users select the Brand Kit in Copilot in PowerPoint and choose a skill from it.
claims.quote: Choose the Brand kit that contains your skill. With the Brand kit selected, select +, and then select Choose skills. You should see your added skill in the skills drop-down.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A Brand Kit skill is available for use by people who have shared access to that kit.
claims.quote: Once added, your brand skill is ready for anyone who has shared access to the Brand kit.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Adding a skill requires a Brand Kit the user owns or has shared editing access to.
claims.quote: Select a Brand kit that you own or have shared editing access to.

claims.claim: Brand Kit skill uploads support .md and .zip files.
claims.quote: Uploaded skills can be a .md file or a .zip file.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Brand Kit skill instructions link to the custom-skill format guidance.
claims.quote: For skill format guidance, see Use custom skills with Copilot in PowerPoint.

claims.claim: A skill supplies reusable written instructions and task guidance to Copilot.
claims.quote: Skills are reusable, instruction-based capabilities that provide agents with domain expertise, workflows, and task-specific guidance.

claims.claim: The brand kit governance page lists logos, colour palettes, fonts, images and templates as kit contents.
claims.quote: Brand kits can include logos, color palettes, fonts, images, and templates.

claims.claim: Two policies govern personal brand kit creation and official brand kit publishing and management.
claims.quote: Brand kit policies control who can create personal brand kits and who can publish or manage official brand kits.

claims.claim: The cited brand kit governance page does not mention skills.
claims.quote: Searched: skills in the full fetched Configure brand kit governance and organizational assets page; it documents kit policies and assets without mentioning skills.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes dated 6 October 2026 list user-defined custom skills in PowerPoint on Windows.
claims.quote:
October 06, 2026
PowerPoint
Create custom skills in Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows]
What changed: Copilot now supports user defined custom skills

claims.claim: Brand Kit sharing grants people, groups or everyone in the organisation Can edit or Can view access.
claims.quote: To share a Brand Kit, select Share, search for people or groups (or turn on Share with everyone in my organization), choose Can edit or Can view, and then select Save changes.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Only brand managers can edit official Brand Kits.
claims.quote: Once a Brand Kit has been made official, only brand managers can make edits and changes to the Brand Kit.

claims.claim: The documented Brand Kit policies govern kit creation and editing, including restrictions on shared editors.
claims.quote: If a user who isn't in the permitted group receives a shared brand kit with edit rights, the user can only view the kit.

claims.claim: Membership of the mail-enabled security groups specified in the policies grants policy access.
claims.quote: Group membership grants policy access.

claims.claim: Group ownership alone does not grant permission to publish or edit official brand kits.
claims.quote: Group owners can manage the group, but ownership alone doesn't grant permission to publish or edit official brand kits.

claims.claim: The body of a custom skill tells Copilot how to do the task.
claims.quote: The body section is your instructions, telling Copilot how to do the task.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state the storage location of uploaded Brand Kit skill files.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Brand kit" "skill" "stored"; opened Brand Skill support, custom skills, official Brand Kits and access guidance. OneDrive storage is documented for personal uploads, not Brand Kit uploads.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state raw file-read permissions for Brand Kit skill files.
claims.quote: Searched: "Brand kit" skill storage file permissions audit; opened Brand Skill support and Brand Kit access guidance. They describe skill use and kit editing/viewing, not raw skill-file read permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described whether a Brand Kit skill can reference files.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Brand kit" "skill" "reference files"; opened Brand Skill support and custom skills. The latter lists ZIP file types but does not state Brand Kit skill file-reference behaviour.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether users see a Brand Kit skill's text before it runs.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Brand kit" "skill" "see" "text"; opened Brand Skill support and custom skills. Editing and choosing skills are documented, but a pre-run display of the text is not.

claims.claim: No source says the arrival of Brand Kit skills changes existing brand kits.
claims.quote: Searched: "Brand kit" skills rollout existing kits automatically; opened Brand Skill support, official Brand Kits and access guidance. They describe adding skills and choosing kits, not automatically changing existing kits.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) allows PowerPoint Copilot use without the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence gives access to the full Copilot in PowerPoint experience.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The official Brand Kits support page says the feature requires a Microsoft Copilot Premium licence.
claims.quote: This feature requires a Microsoft Copilot Premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Brand Kit access guidance requires a work or school account with a Copilot add-on licence for Microsoft 365 to create kits.
claims.quote: To create Brand Kits in Copilot Create, you need to sign in with a work or school (Microsoft Entra ID) account that has a Copilot add-on license for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The feature is included within the named licence for Brand Kits rather than documented as a separately purchased skill entitlement.
claims.quote:
This feature requires a Microsoft Copilot Premium license.
Brand Kit skills allow you to share skills with anyone who has access to the Brand Kit.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no meter for Brand Kit skills at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Brand kit" skills pricing meter credits licensing; "Brand kit" "skills" "meter". Opened Copilot overview, official Brand Kits and Brand Skill support; none names a Brand Kit skill meter.

claims.claim: The brand kit governance page lists an organisation assets library as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Before users can create and publish brand kits, complete the following prerequisites: Create an organization assets library to connect to Copilot.

claims.claim: The governance page requires an administrator with privileges to manage groups and policy configurations.
claims.quote: Make sure that you're an administrator with the privileges required to manage groups and policy configurations.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites for brand kits; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: The prerequisites list separate mail-enabled security groups for brand managers and personal kit creators.
claims.quote: Create a separate mail-enabled security group for brand managers who can publish and manage official brand kits. Create a mail-enabled security group for users who can create and edit personal brand kits.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is the recommended role for managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended)

claims.claim: Security Administrator is supported for accessing and managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: You can use the following built-in Microsoft Entra roles for accessing and managing the feature: ... Security Administrator

claims.claim: Global Administrator is also supported for accessing and managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Global Administrator | This role can manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft services that use Microsoft Entra identities.

claims.claim: Feature-specific rollout mechanics for skills in Brand Kit are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Brand kit" skills rollout existing kits automatically; opened Brand Skill support, official Brand Kits, access guidance and the supplied roadmap. No skill-specific rollout mechanics were found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Brand kit policy changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Policy changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy configuration changes can be searched in the Microsoft Purview audit log.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked. You can use the portal or PowerShell to search the audit log for such changes.

claims.claim: The policies are independent and both checks must be satisfied to publish a personal kit as an official kit.
claims.quote: The policies are independent. To publish a personal brand kit as an official brand kit, a user must satisfy both policy checks.

claims.claim: The brand manager setting must be in a tenant-scoped policy configuration.
claims.quote: Verify that the policy has the following configuration: The policy scope is set to Tenant.

claims.claim: The brand manager policy configuration must have priority 0.
claims.quote: The policy priority is set to 0.

claims.claim: The Graph Tenant Configuration Management list of Copilot Cloud Policy resources contains no brand kit setting.
claims.quote: Searched: brand, kit and Cloud Policy in the fetched Supported Copilot resources for Tenant Configuration Management (preview) reference. No brand kit resource or property is listed.

claims.claim: The official kit policy is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy > Policies > Elevated role for Brand Managers.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Customization > Policy Management. Select an existing tenant-level policy with the scope Apply to all users. ... Select the Policies tab. Search for Brand Manager, and then select Elevated role for Brand Managers.

claims.claim: No API or command is documented for setting the official brand manager policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "brand kit" "Elevated role" API PowerShell Graph policy. Opened brand kit governance, Cloud Policy overview and Graph TCM Copilot resources; no operation setting this policy was found.

claims.claim: Personal kit creation is configured at Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Restrict brand kit creation.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Customization > Policy Management. ... On the Start with the basics page, select Next. On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page: ... Select Restrict brand kit creation.

claims.claim: No API or command is documented for setting Restrict brand kit creation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Restrict brand kit creation" API PowerShell Microsoft Graph. Opened brand kit governance, Cloud Policy overview and Graph TCM Copilot resources; no operation setting this policy was found.

claims.claim: No separate tenant-wide UI or API switch specific to skills in Brand Kit is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Brand kit" skills disable admin policy tenant; "Brand kit" "skills" "policy" disable. Opened Brand Skill support, kit governance, access guidance and Graph TCM Copilot resources; no separate skill switch was found.

claims.claim: Elevated role for Brand Managers should be set to Enabled.
claims.quote: Set the policy to Enabled. By default, the policy is set to Not configured.

claims.claim: The brand manager policy takes the brand manager security group's email address.
claims.quote: In Security group email address, enter the email address of the brand manager security group.

claims.claim: Restrict brand kit creation is configured by setting Configuration setting to Enabled.
claims.quote: In the Restrict brand kit creation pane, set Configuration setting to Enabled.

claims.claim: The personal kit policy takes the permitted creator security group's email address.
claims.quote: Under Additional setting, enter the email address of the security group whose members can create brand kits in Security group email address.

claims.claim: The official kit policy row cautions that the governance page does not say it covers skills.
claims.quote: Enterprise Brand Manager policy | Who can publish, edit, and manage official brand kits.
claims.fix: In controls[0].note and the rendered row, replace 'The page does not say it covers skills.' with 'This policy controls who can publish, edit and manage official brand kits.' The cited policy scope covers kits without excluding those containing skills.

claims.claim: The personal kit policy row cautions that the governance page does not say it covers skills.
claims.quote: Restrict brand kit creation policy | Who can create and edit personal brand kits.
claims.fix: In controls[1].note and the rendered row, replace 'The page does not say it covers skills.' with 'This policy controls who can create and edit personal brand kits.' The cited policy scope covers kits without excluding those containing skills.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Brand Kit skills are a user-opt-in capability.
claims.quote: With the Brand kit selected, select +, and then select Choose skills. You should see your added skill in the skills drop-down. Searched: "Brand kit" skills disable admin policy tenant; no separate skill switch found in governance or Graph TCM references.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review Can edit sharing access, but the controls table has no sharing-permissions row.

claims.fix: Remove the At rollout bullet 'Check which people and groups have **Can edit** access to each shared brand kit, since they can add skills to it.' It names a sharing-permissions control absent from the table; do not add a control row in this correction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to search the Purview audit log, but the controls table has no audit row.
claims.quote: Search the Microsoft Purview audit log for Cloud Policy changes to the brand kit policies. The table contains only the two kit policies and the missing tenant-wide skill switch.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout bullet 'Search the Microsoft Purview audit log for Cloud Policy changes to the brand kit policies.' It names an audit control absent from the table; do not add a control row in this correction.
